children.name: Define how physical keys behave: tap for a key or action, hold to switch layers, or double-tap for extra shortcuts.
A trigger can be a single key or a combination, such as ShiftLeft+ControlLeft. The combination works in either press order and ends when any key is released.
Action performed when the trigger is pressed and released quickly without holding.
Choose a layer active until release, or an action performed once after the hold duration.
Action performed when the trigger is pressed twice quickly within the double-tap timeout.

Any match allows the rule. An empty list allows all windows.

An application is matched by its ID or process name: the whole name, ignoring case, with * and ? as wildcards. A window title item matches when the title contains the text. Any matching item is enough. An empty list imposes no restrictions.
No restrictions: the rule works in every window.

A match blocks the rule, even if the window is in the allowed list.
